candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Deuteronomy
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy, on 8:1-10. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. Mt 4:4, Jn 6:51.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On 'man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord doth man live' (Deu 8:3), Ephrem reads the manna-pedagogy as the canonical anchor cited by Christ at the first Temptation (Mt 4:4 / Lk 4:4 — verbatim citation). The manna teaches that humanity's deepest hunger is for the Word, not for bread; the Eucharist resolves both hungers in one. Tewahedo eucharistic theology cites Deu 8:3 + Jn 6:51 ('I am the living bread which came down from heaven') + Mt 4:4 as the canonical triple-witness: Christ is the Word-who-is-Bread, fulfilling the Deuteronomic pedagogy in the Eucharistic anaphora.
